title: EU commits €28 million to Mozambique digital transformation under Global Gateway
description:
"Digital transformation has been allocated €28 million, with a particular focus on
increasing women's participation in the digital economy." One of four Global Gateway
agreements — clean energy €40m, digital transformation €28m, agricultural businesses and
sustainable value chains €60m, education and skills €50m — totalling €178 million,
described by the source as "the signing of four agreements".

Only the digital transformation slice is recorded here; the energy and agriculture slices
are out of the wiki's scope, and the €50m education and skills line is recorded on the
prose source rather than as a separate digital record because its stated purpose
("to prepare Mozambican students for a digital and sustainable economy") is not specific
enough to a digital activity to map cleanly.

title: Tmcel Telecommunications Network Second Expansion Financing
Laying the Foundation for VaMoz Digital (Mozambique)
description: ITU is implementing agency for the regulatory and policy component of the EU-funded VaMoz Digital! programme in Mozambique. Project strengthens enabling environment for inclusive digital transformation through: policy and regulatory framework reform; institutional capacity development for telecom regulators; digital skills curriculum; and fostering a digital innovation ecosystem. ITU component (Outcome 1) of broader EUR 10M VaMoz Digital! programme (EU Global Gateway flagship). AICS implements complementary youth digital skills component.
recipient_organisation: Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation; INTIC

instrument: Concessional loan *(source label, unverified — see Notes)*
title: Mozambique Digital Acceleration Project
description: Accelerates Mozambique's digital economy through expanded broadband access, digital government services, digital financial infrastructure, and digital skills programs.

title: VaMOZ Digital!
description: Mozambique remains one of the bottom ten countries in the world in terms of human development, aggravated by increasing inequality in recent years, including significant gender differences, Gini-coefficient rose to 0.56 (2014/15) from 0.47 (2008/9), placing Mozambique among the most unequal countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, substantial disparities between North and south and urban versus rural area

title: National Control Centre for Energy
description: The country has set ambitious targets for its energy sector: by 2030, universal access as well as 62% of renewable energy in the energy mix, and 20% of solar and wind generation in 2043. However, these targets are hampered by the fact that Mozambique does not have an appropriate control of its electricity grid. The Mozambican power grid currently comprises two independent and unconnected sub-grids

instrument: Concessional loan *(source label, unverified — see Notes)*
title: Sustainable Energy and Broadband Access in Rural Mozambique Project
description: Expands rural broadband access and provides sustainable energy in Mozambique through shared infrastructure investment. Supports last-mile broadband connectivity alongside rural electrification.

instrument: IDA grant *(corrected from the source's "Concessional loan"; PAD4298 records a grant of SDR 105m, US$150m equivalent)*
title: Digital Governance and Economy Project
description: Supports Mozambique's digital governance and economy through improved digital government platforms, broadband infrastructure, and digital financial services.

title: Vital Statistics in Support of Maternal, Newborn and Child Health \u2014 Mozambique (Phase 2)
description: Phase 2 continuation: accelerates birth and death registration, expands civil registration digital infrastructure, and increases vital statistics data quality in Mozambique to support MNCH outcomes.

title: Modernization and Expansion of the National Mobile Network (Tmcel)
description: Concessional loan to modernize and expand the national mobile telecommunications network of Tmcel (Mozambique Telecom), the state-owned operator. Includes network expansion across multiple phases to improve mobile coverage and service quality nationwide.

title: Vital Statistics in Support of Maternal, Newborn and Child Health \u2014 Mozambique (Phase 1)
description: Increases civil and vital registration rates in Mozambique to improve policies and programs that reduce maternal and child mortality. Includes digital registration technology, mobile data platforms, and vital statistics information systems.
